speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin our assessment, how long have you had this lesion, and does it have a history of trauma or insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and a prior ant bite at the site, I need to determine if this is an infectious complication or a necrotizing skin disease. Do you have any fever, chills, or spreading redness around the lesion, and are you currently taking any immunosuppressive medications for your Crohn's? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and ESR.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a central necrotic base with purplish irregular borders, following an ant bite in a patient with diabetes and Crohn's disease, is highly concerning for ecthyma gangrenosum or a severe necrotizing soft tissue infection. REQUEST TEST: Blood Culture, Gram Stain, and Wound Swab Culture. Do you have any new fever, chills, or a feeling that the pain is out of proportion to the appearance of the skin? REQUEST IMAGES: Right leg lesion close-up.

speaker: Doctor
text: The measurements are normal, but I need to clarify your systemic status: do you currently have a fever, and does the pain in the lesion feel significantly worse than what the skin appearance suggests? REQUEST TEST: Lactate level, Procalcitonin, and Arterial Blood Gas.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of diabetes and Crohn's disease, along with the lesion's necrotic base and purplish borders, we must urgently rule out Pseudomonas ecthyma gangrenosum or necrotizing fasciitis. Please tell me if you are currently experiencing a fever, chills, or if the pain in the leg feels significantly worse than the skin looks. DIAGNOSIS READY: Necrotizing Soft Tissue Infection (suspected Ecthyma Gangrenosum)
